links.comparator_used: The same consent documents left unchanged (original forms)
links.outcome: Readability grade level and content fidelity (precision, recall, F1) of LLM-simplified consent forms
links.effect: Grade level fell from 14.1 ± 1.3 to 8.8 ± 1.2 after first LLM revision (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction; second revision 9.9 ± 1.2 (P = 0.87, no further improvement). Mean F1 0.71 ± 0.26, precision 0.95 ± 0.06, recall 0.62 ± 0.16. Greater reading-level reductions were associated with decreased fidelity (r = 0.73, P < 0.01).
links.tradeoff: Substantial content omissions (lower recall) despite few hallucinations; greater simplification linked to lower fidelity; readability did not reach the sixth-grade target; human review needed.
links.quote: LLM-based editing significantly improved consent form readability but resulted in substantial content omissions.

design_hint: reading-level constraint with human review of LLM-simplified consent forms
